amendment.text: Omaha does not use the state's table (Uniform Plumbing Code Table 422.1). Its building code sends plumbing to Chapter 49 of the Omaha Municipal Code, the city's own plumbing code, whose Section 49-722 holds ten fixture tables by kind of building. Total occupancy is divided by two (one man to one woman) and each half is read against the table. Offices use Table 49-722(5A) for floor area per person (professional offices 160 sq ft, common areas left out) and Table 49-722(5B) for fixtures, with separate columns for men's toilets and men's urinals. The table whose notes speak of restaurants, Table 49-722(3), counts 15 sq ft per person after deducting kitchens, restrooms, bar areas and similar, and treats a restaurant serving alcohol with meals as one that doesn't; establishments serving liquor have a stricter Table 49-722(4). Schools use Table 49-722(8A): one toilet per 25 elementary students, per 30 secondary students, per 15 in preschool, counted per floor at 35 sq ft per student, with staff toilets separate and additional under Table 49-722(5B). After the first men's toilet and urinal, two urinals may be provided for each toilet. In multi-storey buildings the count is made floor by floor. Assembly and retail buildings needing six or more toilets and urinals must add a family restroom.
amendment.quote: Sec. 49-720: Fixture requirements shall then be determined by referencing occupancy groupings in section 49-721, the corresponding table in section 49-722 and the following: Once the total occupancy has been calculated, divide the total by two, assuming a one-to-one ratio of males to females. Apply the resulting numbers to the tables in section 49-722 [...] Ratios other than one to one, males to females, shall be submitted to the plumbing board for approval. When the minimum requirement for males of one WC and one UR are met, the ratio may be two UR for each WC thereafter. | Table 49-722(5B) Number / WC Male / UR Male / Lav Male / WC Female / Lav Female: 1-5: 1,0,1,1,1; 6-10: 1,0,1,2,1; 11-25: 1,1,1,3,2; 26-50: 1,1,1,4,2; 51-75: 2,2,2,5,3; 76-100: 3,2,3,6,3; 101-150: 4,3,4,7,4; 151-200: 5,3,4,8,4; 201-250: 6,4,5,9,5; 251-300: 7,4,6,10,5. Above 300: Males: Add one water closet or one urinal for each additional 50 or fraction thereof. Females: Add one water closet for each additional 50 or fraction thereof. | Table 49-722(3) Number / WC Male / UR Male / Lav Male / WC Female / Lav Female / DF: 1-25: 1,0,1,1,1,0; 26-50: 1,0,1,2,1,1; 51-75: 1,1,1,3,2,1; 76-100: 1,1,1,4,2,1; 101-200: 2,1,2,5,3,2; 201-300: 2,2,2,6,3,3. Note 2: Any restaurant that serves alcoholic beverages or liquor for consumption on premises as part of the meal served shall be considered as a restaurant that does not serve alcoholic beverages. Note 3: Occupant load shall be based on 15 square feet per person after deducting areas such as stairwells, restrooms, entries, elevators, dance floors, kitchen, bar areas, and utility rooms. | Table 49-722(8A) Per Floor / WC / Lav / DF / MS: Preschool/nursery 1 per 15; Elementary 1 per 25; Secondary 1 per 30; College/University 1 per 35. Note 1: Under Table 49-722(8A) the occupant load factor is 35 sq. ft. per students. Note 3: For children six years of age and under, a unisex restroom may be used. For children over seven years of age, separate accommodations shall be provided. Note 4: Facilities for school staff shall be separate and in addition to those for the students using Table 49-722(5B).

worked_examples.how: 50 occupants, divided by two = 25 per sex. Table 49-722(5B), row 11-25: men 1 toilet and 1 urinal, women 3 toilets.
50 per sex. Table 49-722(5B), row 26-50: men 1 toilet and 1 urinal, women 4 toilets.
100 per sex. Table 49-722(5B), row 76-100: men 3 toilets and 2 urinals, women 6 toilets.
200 per sex. Table 49-722(5B), row 151-200: men 5 toilets and 3 urinals, women 8 toilets.
25 per sex. Table 49-722(3), row 1-25: men 1 toilet, no urinal; women 1 toilet.
50 per sex. Table 49-722(3), row 26-50: men 1 toilet, no urinal; women 2 toilets.
100 per sex. Table 49-722(3), row 76-100: men 1 toilet and 1 urinal; women 4 toilets.
200 per sex. Table 49-722(3), row 101-200: men 2 toilets and 1 urinal; women 5 toilets.
25 students per sex at 1 toilet per 25 = 1 each. Table 49-722(8A) has one WC column and no urinal column; rounding up of fractions is our assumption (the table does not say).
50 per sex / 25 = 2 each. Secondary at 1 per 30: 1.67, 2 each.
100 per sex / 25 = 4 each. Secondary at 1 per 30: 3.33, 4 each.
200 per sex / 25 = 8 each. Secondary at 1 per 30: 6.67, 7 each. Under Sec. 49-720(c) some of the boys' fixtures may be urinals.

That Table 49-722(3) is the restaurant table, (4) the table for establishments serving liquor, (5A)/(5B) the business table and (8A) the school table is taken from the tables' own notes and row labels.
Whether the 'Number' column means occupants of one sex follows from Sec. 49-720(b)(1) ('divide the total by two [...] Apply the resulting numbers to the tables').
How Table 49-722(8A) (one WC column, per floor) is split between boys and girls, and how fractions round, is not stated in the text read.

restrooms_city.rule: Omaha's plumbing code sets its own restroom rules in place of the state code's. Where both sexes are employed or served, separate restrooms are required, each marked 'Men's' or 'Gentlemen' and 'Women's' or 'Ladies' in letters at least two inches high or with international symbols, and the code says no person shall be allowed to use a restroom assigned to the other gender. A 'unisex restroom' is a separate lockable room with a toilet, a lavatory and a urinal, accessible, labeled 'Unisex Restroom' (two-inch letters or a symbol) with an occupied/unoccupied sign; a room labeled Men or Women may not serve as one. Unisex restrooms may not be installed at swimming pools, in schools (except the nurse's office and for children five and under), in malls, or where food or drinks are prepared or served (except a carry-out business of 750 sq ft or less with no seating and four or fewer employees). A single unisex restroom may serve a business under 2,000 gross sq ft with four or fewer employees. Assembly and retail buildings that need six or more toilets and urinals must add a family use restroom. The sections read make no provision for a shared multi-stall all-gender room.
restrooms_city.quote: Sec. 49-704: Where two genders are employed or accommodated, separate restrooms shall be provided and utilized according to the following provisions (exception: see section 49-708): [...] Each restroom shall be distinctly marked with regard to gender. No person shall be allowed to use a restroom assigned to the other gender. The door or room labels shall be the words "Men's" or "Gentlemen", "Women's" or "Ladies", respectively, in letters not less than two inches in height, or other international symbols. | Sec. 49-708: The minimum fixture requirement for unisex restrooms shall be one water closet, one lavatory, and one urinal. (Exception: As noted in subsections (e) and (f). A restroom labeled "Men" or "Women" shall not serve as a unisex restroom). Unisex restrooms shall not be installed in the following facilities: Swimming pools. Schools [...] Malls [...] Where food or drinks are prepared or served. [...] A single unisex restroom is allowed where at least one of the following conditions applies: The gross area of the space occupied by a business where four or fewer employees are normally stationed is less than 2,000 gross square feet. [...] General requirements for unisex restrooms: Shall have a lockable door. Shall meet all disability accessibility requirements. The door or room shall be labeled accordingly: "Unisex Restroom" in letters minimum two inches in height, or other international symbol. A sign indicating whether the room is occupied or unoccupied.

partition_rules_city.text: Each toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door, at least 30 inches wide and 60 inches long. A partition is required between any urinal and a lavatory. Toilets: 15 inches from the centre to any wall or partition, 31 inches centre to centre.
partition_rules_city.quote: Sec. 49-732 Water Closet Compartment (Partitions): Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partition and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. The minimum size stall or compartment shall be 30 inches in width and 60 inches in length. Exceptions: Water closet compartments shall not be required in a single occupant toilet room with a lockable door. Toilet rooms located in day care and child care facilities and containing two or more water closets shall be permitted to have one water closet without an enclosing compartment. | Sec. 49-730: Water closets. 15 inches from the center of the fixture to any wall, partition or vanity. [...] 31 inches from the center of one water closet to the center of any other water closet or urinal. [...] Urinals. There shall be a minimum of 15 inches from the center of the urinal to any wall or partition. [...] There shall be a partition between any urinal and lavatory.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Omaha job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see Omaha's own stall counts and restroom rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Omaha offices, schools, hospitals and warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use, and a room with six or more toilets and urinals also needs a narrower stall with grab bars on both sides. Federal law sets the sizes, and Nebraska's own access rules adopt the federal ones. In Omaha the city checks plans for commercial work against them, and a building can't get its occupancy permit until it complies.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Omaha's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) and polypropylene partitions to pass a room-corner fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Omaha has its own plumbing rules, separate from Nebraska's, and they set the number of toilets and urinals by the kind of building and how many people use it. The table below shows what that means.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Stall size:** in Omaha every toilet used by the public or by employees needs its own stall with a door, at least 30 inches wide and 60 inches long. A partition is also required between a urinal and a sink.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** Omaha's rules call for separate men's and women's restrooms, each marked for one sex, and say no person may use a restroom assigned to the other. A "unisex restroom" under Omaha's rules is a lockable one-person room with a toilet, a sink and a urinal, a "Unisex Restroom" sign or symbol and a sign showing whether it is occupied. One such room can serve a business of under 2,000 square feet with four or fewer employees. Unisex rooms aren't allowed at swimming pools, in malls, in places that serve food or drink or, with narrow exceptions, in schools. Places of assembly and stores that need six or more toilets and urinals must add a family restroom. The rules don't provide for a shared all-gender room with stalls, so ask Omaha Permits and Inspections before planning one.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** ask Omaha Permits and Inspections (402-444-5350) whether replacing or adding partitions in an existing restroom needs a building permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Omaha counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and each half is read against the city's table for that kind of building. Every toilet needs a stall. In offices and larger restaurants the men's room needs urinals as well as toilets, and the women's room needs more toilets than the men's.
page.stalls_after: The restaurant column also covers restaurants that serve alcohol with meals. Bars and other places serving liquor follow a stricter table, and outdoor seating counts once it passes a quarter of the indoor seats. The school column counts students only, at one toilet for every 25 elementary students. Secondary schools need one for every 30, and staff toilets are separate and extra. Omaha's school table doesn't say how many of the boys' fixtures may be urinals, so confirm the split with Omaha Permits and Inspections. In a building with several floors, Omaha counts each floor on its own. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Omaha's plumbing rules count a professional office at one person per 160 square feet, leaving out break rooms, lobbies and other shared areas. A restaurant is counted at one person per 15 square feet after taking out the kitchen, bar, restrooms and entries, and a school at one student per 35 square feet. Your architect or Omaha Permits and Inspections sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Check local contractor licensing or registration with Omaha Permits and Inspections before work starts. Nebraska has no state contractor license: installers working on other people's property register with the Nebraska Department of Labor, with proof of workers' compensation cover if they have employees. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Nebraska that contractor registers with the state Department of Labor, and you check Omaha's own licensing rule with Omaha Permits and Inspections.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Nebraska does not set wage rates for public jobs: state law has contractors bidding on public works confirm that they pay what at least half of the contractors in their trade pay. Where federal money is involved, the federal rate applies: $33.42 an hour plus $18.66 in benefits for a carpenter on building work in Douglas County.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7% in Omaha: 5.5% state and 1.5% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and medical campuses:** stainless steel or phenolic where restrooms are disinfected often.

sources: - Codes Omaha enforces: [Omaha Building Code 2018](https://up.codes/viewer/omaha/ibc-2018) (2018 International Building Code with Omaha amendments, Omaha Municipal Code Chapter 43; its Chapter 29 reads "Plumbing systems shall be installed in accordance with Chapter 49 of the Omaha Municipal Code") and the [Omaha Plumbing Code](https://up.codes/viewer/omaha/om-plumbing-code) (Omaha Municipal Code Chapter 49, Ordinance No. 40524 of October 20, 2015, amended by Ordinance No. 42654 of August 13, 2021), both read on UpCodes, a secondary copy; list of Omaha codes and dates at [UpCodes, Omaha Building Codes](https://up.codes/codes/omaha). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet and urinal counts in Omaha: Omaha Municipal Code [Section 49-722, Fixture Requirement Tables](https://up.codes/s/fixture-requirement-tables) (Tables 49-722(3), (4), (5A), (5B) and (8A) with their notes), [Section 49-720, Determining Fixture Count](https://up.codes/s/determining-fixture-count) and [Section 49-703, Minimum Facilities for Occupied Nonresidential Buildings](https://up.codes/s/minimum-facilities-for-occupied-nonresidential-buildings), read on UpCodes. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Stall size and the partition between urinal and sink: Omaha Municipal Code [Section 49-732, Water Closet Compartment (Partitions)](https://up.codes/s/water-closet-compartment-partitions) and [Section 49-730, Space Requirement for Non-Handicapped Plumbing Fixtures](https://up.codes/s/space-requirement-for-non-handicapped-plumbing-fixtures), read on UpCodes. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Separate, unisex and family restrooms in Omaha: Omaha Municipal Code [Section 49-704, Provide Restrooms for Two Genders](https://up.codes/s/provide-restrooms-for-two-genders), [Section 49-708, Unisex Restrooms](https://up.codes/s/unisex-restrooms) and [Section 49-705, Right of Use of Restrooms in Businesses by Customers](https://up.codes/s/right-of-use-of-restrooms-in-businesses-by-customers), read on UpCodes. No state restroom-use law: [LB 89 (2025), Stand With Women Act, as enacted](https://www.nebraskalegislature.gov/FloorDocs/109/PDF/Slip/LB89.pdf) and [LB 730 (2026), Nebraska Legislature bill page](https://www.nebraskalegislature.gov/bills/view_bill.php?DocumentID=62661) (indefinitely postponed). - Fire test for solid plastic partitions and wheelchair-access counts in Omaha's building code: Omaha Building Code 2018, [Sections 803.9 and 803.1.1 (NFPA 286)](https://up.codes/viewer/omaha/ibc-2018/chapter/8/interior-finishes) and [Section 1109.2](https://up.codes/viewer/omaha/ibc-2018/chapter/11/accessibility), read on UpCodes. Checked 2026-11-24.
